title: How the kingdom is remembered
hook: Sikhs remember it with pride and also discuss its failings

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Samadhi in Lahore, and your line, remembered in stone. Today, memory that isn't made of stone, and the week closes.

A family dinner somewhere in the Punjab, or in Toronto, or in Birmingham. A grandfather is talking about Maharaja Ranjit Singh, the Lion of the Punjab, and the time when a Sikh flag flew over Lahore. His granddaughter has been reading too. She asks about the court's killings, the queens on the pyre, the ministers who sold each other out. For a moment the table goes quiet. Then the grandfather nods. Both of them are telling the truth.
screen: `A GRANDFATHER AND THE LION OF THE PUNJAB.` → `A GRANDDAUGHTER'S HARD QUESTIONS.` → `BOTH ARE TELLING THE TRUTH.`

segments.voice: For many Sikhs, the kingdom of Ranjit Singh is a time when the Khalsa that had been hunted ruled in its own name. The Harmandir shone with gold, coins carried the Gurus' names, a court of many faiths served one Maharaja, and mercy was part of his memory. Songs, paintings and family stories keep that alive. Sikh writers and teachers also talk openly about what went wrong. The Maharaja was rebuked at the Akal Takht for his own conduct. His court was full of rivals. After his death, plots killed his heirs and ministers, and the army grew louder than the throne. And the queens and servants who died on his pyre are part of the story too. Why do the Gurus make room for both? In a hymn of Guru Nanak in Sri Rag, he says truth is higher than everything, and higher still is truthful living. That sets a hard standard for remembering. A memory that only boasts isn't fully true, and neither is one that only blames. Look back at this week: the Maharaja's death, two heirs lost in a year, Sher Singh and the ministers, a child on the throne, the soldiers' councils, a samadhi of stone, and now this. A hard week of the story. Holding pride and honesty at once is how a community keeps a kingdom without pretending about it.
screen: `THE PRIDE: THE KHALSA RULED.` · `THE FAILINGS, SAID OPENLY.` · `TRUTHFUL LIVING, HIGHER STILL.` · `A WEEK OF A HARD STORY.` · then, large: `PRIDE AND HONESTY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind something you belong to and care about, a family, a town, a team, a community, and let one thing you're proud of come forward; rest with it a few breaths. Then, gently, let one honest failing come forward too, and let them sit side by side, like two people at the same table. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out.
Sach, truth. Guru Nanak says truth is higher than everything, and truthful living higher still, the standard for remembering a kingdom honestly.
Your line: pride and honesty. At that table, both of them were telling the truth. Seven more days, walked.
